### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/service-settings`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **59** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/system.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**20** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json eff90af6a2a68202ef167b8ed91aadecfaed90b7`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/system.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **9** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **64** of **227** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **175** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json eff90af6a2a68202ef167b8ed91aadecfaed90b7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b915065c3d196cc31098588669d05006b99d7125` — the merge of head `32b54d4d94b4d90ab561fe62098cba565e4ad421` into base `eff90af6a2a68202ef167b8ed91aadecfaed90b7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b915065c3d196cc31098588669d05006b99d7125 && git checkout b915065c3d196cc31098588669d05006b99d7125
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin eff90af6a2a68202ef167b8ed91aadecfaed90b7 32b54d4d94b4d90ab561fe62098cba565e4ad421 && git checkout -B drift-repro eff90af6a2a68202ef167b8ed91aadecfaed90b7 && git merge --no-ff 32b54d4d94b4d90ab561fe62098cba565e4ad421

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json eff90af6a2a68202ef167b8ed91aadecfaed90b7
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs eff90af6a2a68202ef167b8ed91aadecfaed90b7` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review (Fable) — PR #31386 @ 32b54d4d

Verdict: PASS

Scope reviewed: `packages/spec/src/system/settings-manifest.zod.ts` (enum :58, column kind/column/key-column sub-schemas :84-116, `keyColumn`/`columns` slots and stored-shape doc :592-611, superRefine map block :680-720) and `settings-manifest.test.ts:198-261`; `packages/spec/authorable-surface/system.json:1143,1153`; `content/docs/references/system/settings-manifest.mdx`; `docs/adr/0007-settings-manifest-and-kv-store.md:3,109,125-126`; `packages/services/service-settings/src/map-shape.ts` (`declaredMapShape` :44-54, `firstMapShapeMiss` :83-112, `cellFits` :114-117, `mapMissSentence` :133-158); `settings-service.ts` (`MAP_MISS_CODES` :823-829, `maps` registry :928-929/:1380-1388, env audit :1453-1455, option-family skip :1525-1527, env map branch :1620-1635, `mapShapeVerdict` :1975-1988, `servedManifest` :1998-2017, save-door map branch :3606-3627, `coerceEnvValue` :4507); `packages/objectql/src/lifecycle/lifecycle-key-options.ts:57-82` and its test :26-133; `lifecycle-settings.ts:44-83`; `plugin.ts:1220-1233`; `settings-map-shape-30208.test.ts:55-281`. Judged by reading only; the suite was not run here.

### Findings

**nit** — An *empty* authoritative key answer admits every key. `mapShapeVerdict` (settings-service.ts:1984) builds `admitsKey` only when `allowed.length > 0`, so a reachable registry that declares no lifecycle object (or a source answering `{ options: [] }`) admits any key. The stated fallback covers the source being *unavailable* (pinned, `lifecycle-key-options.test.ts:62-64`), not "answered none". This follows the option-family precedent (:1532), so it is not a contract breach, but the ruling's wording argues for fail-closed. Fix: pass `admitsKey` whenever `optionSourceAnswer` returned an answer (empty included), and keep the `allowed.length > 0` gate only for the declared-table fallback. Pin: a registry of `[]` lifecycle objects, save `{ quotas: { sys_audit_log: 1 } }` ⇒ `invalid_option`.

**nit** — Two refusal classes are unpinned. (1) An array value: `isPlainRecord` (map-shape.ts:175-179) refuses it as `not_a_map`, but the only `not_a_map` pin is JSON text. Pin `save({ quotas: [] })` ⇒ `invalid_type`. (2) A scalar entry in a several-column map (`{ sys_job_run: '1y' }` ⇒ `not_an_entry` at :98); only the empty-object form is pinned. Low value and also unpinned: the column-name identifier regex (zod.ts:99), and the held-verdict path for a map key (:1627). Because `firstMapShapeMiss` stops at the first miss, a held key miss on one entry hides a cell miss on another until the seal. The reader tolerates bad cells, so that is cosmetic.

**nit** — Outside scope, but it contradicts the amendment: `lifecycle-service.ts:1161` still says "These keys are `json` specifiers". One-line comment fix.

### Checked and fine

- **Schema:** `map` is a closed-enum, value-bearing member. It refuses no `keyColumn`, no or empty `columns`, duplicate column names, a `kind` outside `duration|positive_integer`, and `keyColumn`/`columns` on any other type; each is pinned. **`map` is the right name:** it matches the stored `Record<key, …>` and the ADR row, whereas `keyed_rows` describes the rendering and `table` collides with data tables.
- **Stored-shape rule:** stated in the spec doc, the mdx, the ADR row and `lifecycle-settings.ts`, and enforced by `firstMapShapeMiss`. `lifecycle-service.ts` has no diff; `loadGovernance` reads the same shapes. Zero migration holds.
- **Pure widening:** both new slots are optional, and no specifier at the merge base declares `columns`/`keyColumn`, so no existing manifest is invalidated.
- **ADR amendment:** status line, a dated paragraph under "New types require an ADR amendment", the `map` row, and the `json` row annotated. It is minimal and consistent with the closed-set rule, and the escape-hatch text is untouched.
- **One judgement, both doors:** save (:3606-3627) and env (:1620-1635) both call `mapShapeVerdict` → `firstMapShapeMiss`, with the domain taken from `optionTableOf`. There is no bypass: env text goes through `coerceEnvValue`, the whole-value option check is skipped for maps, sourced map keys are judged on read, and the seal re-runs `effectiveEnvOverride`. Codes are stable, sentences name key, entry, column and expected form, and strings are described by length only.
- **Cascade / locks / per-org:** untouched, and `retention_overrides` stays `scope: 'tenant'`.
- **Option source:** the domain is derived at call time (lifecycle class ≠ `record`, the sweep's own set). Gaining or losing `lifecycle` is pinned, and the source is registered before the manifest, pinned over a real kernel. The manifest declares no key list.
- **Ablations:** the dev's three ablations are consistent with the pins. The positive-integer case, JSON text, an unknown column and an empty entry are pinned on the save door.
- **Known gaps:** English column labels are `I18nLabelSchema`, so the ui card can supply translations without a spec change. Checking retention columns against each object's declared policy is outside ruling A.

## Contract review — ACCEPT

Head-sha: `32b54d4d94b4d90ab561fe62098cba565e4ad421`

**ACCEPT · Fable 6717755004 (PASS, nits only ⇒ no delta review) + in-seat review of the rest · 2026-11-08T05:31Z**

- **The contract follows ruling A** (record 6715997428, 田騏 「同意」 2026-11-08 02:07Z), and it keeps all six hard constraints. `map` is added to `SpecifierType` with `keyColumn`/`columns`. Stored shapes are unchanged: a single column stores scalars, several store objects. One judgement, `firstMapShapeMiss` via `mapShapeVerdict`, serves both the save door and the env door. The key domain comes from runtime option sources (lifecycle class ≠ `record`), and the manifest holds no list. `json` stays for raw config. The JSON examples are removed from the ten packs that carried them and from the English manifest text. The ui control is a separate card (the seat files it). Fable confirms the name `map`.
- **Fable's nits are not blocking and are carried as a follow-up**, recorded on #30208 and in the seat's handoff brief: an empty source answer should fail closed, an array value and a scalar entry need pins, and the `lifecycle-service.ts:1161` comment still says `json`.
- **The seat's own read (outside Fable's scope) finds nothing to fix.** That covers the changeset (spec `minor`, services `patch`, both declaration lines, BREAKING with migration, one ADR-0087 marker), the BREAKING note in the body, the ten translation packs, `config-resolution.mdx`, the strictness-ledger count (397 → 399, regenerated) and the `Skills-docs:` line (no skill teaches the specifier set or the keys' value form, which checks out).
- **Gates on `32b54d4d` (report 6717706756):** 121 derived, all exit 0, `--ran` 0 NOT-MEASURED. Full dogfood: 437 files passed, 3 skipped; 3618 tests passed, 41 skipped; exit 0. The spec, objectql and service-settings suites, typecheck and lint all pass. Ablations B1–B3 went red, then were restored.
- **Landing:** this PR touches a governed surface (`docs/adr/**`), so it is Tier H and waits for the maintainer's merge; it is under 3000 lines. The seat readies it and requests review.
